subject: general
question: The Green Revolution in India primarily led to an increase in the production of which crops?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat and Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India began in the 1960s and primarily focused on increasing agricultural productivity through the use of high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, irrigation, fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• Wheat and rice were the major crops targeted under the Green Revolution due to their importance as staple food crops in India.
 
• The introduction of HYV seeds for wheat in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh significantly boosted production, making India self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• Rice production also saw a notable increase, especially in regions with suitable irrigation facilities, contributing to food security in the country.
 
• The Green Revolution helped India overcome food shortages and reduce dependency on imports during the 1960s and 1970s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yield Variety (HYV) Seeds:** These seeds were the backbone of the Green Revolution, offering higher productivity compared to traditional seeds.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** The Green Revolution not only improved food grain production but also boosted the rural economy and reduced poverty in several regions.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** The intensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides led to soil degradation and water pollution, raising concerns about long-term sustainability.
 
• **Regional Disparities:** The benefits of the Green Revolution were concentrated in states like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh, leading to regional inequalities in agricultural development.
 
• **Role of Irrigation:** Efficient irrigation systems like canal and tube wells were crucial for the success of the Green Revolution, especially in areas with low rainfall.
